title: Socket timeout/restart may repeat committed progress
mechanism: Socket syscall handlers map EINTR to ERESTARTSYS unconditionally, and handle_pending_signal rewinds the syscall under SA_RESTART, so timed socket calls restart and any path returning EINTR after committed progress would repeat it.
contract: With SA_RESTART, socket calls that have a timeout set fail with EINTR instead of restarting, and an interrupted call that already transferred data returns the partial count (signal(7)).
observed: Source only: timed socket calls are restarted, as FIXMEs acknowledge. No backend was found that returns EINTR after committed progress.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an SO_RCVTIMEO recv interrupted by an SA_RESTART signal and a patterned large send interrupted repeatedly.

caveats: Broad restart question. AST-26 rejection applies only to regular files. Open PR #3576 covers the timeout part only partially and is unmerged. No committed-progress replay path was established.
